extraction.name: ARC (AI2 Reasoning Challenge)
extraction.description: A new question set, text corpus, and baselines assembled to encourage AI research in advanced question answering. The dataset contains 7,787 natural, grade-school science questions partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set.
extraction.creator: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord
extraction.citeAs: Clark, P., Cowhey, I., Etzioni, O., Khot, T., Sabharwal, A., Schoenick, C., & Tafjord, O. (2018). Think you have Solved Question Answering? Try ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge. arXiv preprint arXiv:1803.05457.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions were authored for use on standardized tests. The dataset was assembled through several months of extensive search and investigation. Sources include various state assessments and an anonymous content partner.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions were drawn from a variety of sources including state assessments (e.g., ACTAAP, AIMS, FCAT, MCAS, NY Regents) and an anonymous content partner (Mercury).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were partitioned into Challenge Set and Easy Set based on whether they were answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based algorithm and a word co-occurrence algorithm.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were authored for human tests; no additional annotation was performed for the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The Challenge Set is designed to be hard for retrieval and co-occurrence methods; none of the baseline systems tested significantly outperform random baseline on the Challenge Set.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation; intended for advanced question answering research.
